data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise when no article is used with general plural nouns, uncountable nouns, languages, meals and common expressions.
data.learningTitle: Knowing When to Use No Article
learningPoints: Use no article with plural nouns when speaking generally.
Use no article with uncountable nouns when speaking generally.
Use no article with most languages and school subjects.
Use no article with meals such as breakfast, lunch and dinner in general use.
Recognise common expressions such as go to school and go to bed.
Contrast zero article with 'the' when the meaning becomes specific.

sections.summary: Using no article with plural nouns in general.
sections.explain: Plural countable nouns take no article when speaking about the whole class in general.

words.word: Dogs are friendly animals.
The dogs are friendly animals.
A dogs are friendly animals.

sections.summary: Using no article with an uncountable noun in general.
sections.explain: Uncountable nouns often take no article when speaking generally.

words.word: Water is important for life.
The water is important for life.
A water is important for life.

sections.explain: Most language names are used without an article.

words.word: She speaks Spanish.
She speaks the Spanish.
She speaks a Spanish.

sections.explain: BREAKFAST, LUNCH and DINNER usually take no article when referring to the meal generally.

words.word: We have dinner at seven.
We have the dinner at seven.
We have a dinner at seven every day.

sections.summary: Using no article in 'go to school'.
sections.explain: Use no article with SCHOOL when referring to its normal purpose.

words.word: The children go to school at eight.
The children go to the school at eight.
The children go to a school at eight.

sections.summary: Using no article in 'go to bed'.
sections.explain: BED takes no article in the expression GO TO BED.

words.word: I usually go to bed at eleven.
I usually go to the bed at eleven.
I usually go to a bed at eleven.

sections.summary: Using no article with a school subject.
sections.explain: School subjects normally take no article.

words.word: Maths is difficult for me.
The maths is difficult for me.
A maths is difficult for me.

sections.explain: Use THE when referring to specific things already identified, but no article for things in general.

words.word: I like music, but the music in this café is too loud.
I like the music, but music in this café is too loud.
I like a music, but the music in this café is too loud.

sections.summary: Using no article with a general activity.
sections.explain: Many activities and abstract nouns take no article when used generally.

words.word: Exercise is good for you.
The exercise is good for you.
An exercise is good for you.

sections.summary: Using no article with plural food nouns generally.
sections.explain: Use no article with plural nouns when talking about them generally.

words.word: Vegetables are good for you.
The vegetables are good for you.
A vegetables are good for you.
